results.reason: Issue 1 says the Renewal Notice deadline of about Aug. 16, 2026 has passed and the Schedule note shows no notice was delivered. It says the DA expires Nov. 14, 2026, before the Nov. 30 closing. It calls the MIPA §3.12(c) 'through November 2029' rep untrue and explains the Sellers' indemnity and fraud exposure.

Issue 2 says the 100% sale is a Change of Control requiring Velloran's prior written consent under DA §14.2, with an immediate termination right (§14.3/15.4). It notes the consent is omitted from Sched. 3.6 and so falls outside the §6.4 covenant and the §7.1(d) condition. It recommends obtaining the consent now and adding it to Sched. 3.6.

Issue 4 says SL §1.1 adds New York and Virginia, so the non-compete and 18-month tail cover six states while exclusivity covers four. It notes the SL outranks the DA body under §19.4. It recommends conforming the territory or extending exclusivity to NY and VA.

Issue 6 says SL §6 selects New York law and exclusive New York County courts, conflicting with DA §18.1–18.2 (Delaware law, Wilmington courts). It explains that one dispute could be split across two states under two laws. It recommends conforming the SL to Delaware law and forum.
The memo states the Initial Term ends Nov. 14, 2026 (DA §3.1) and identifies the DA as dated Nov. 15, 2023.
The memo states the target closing is Nov. 30, 2026 (MIPA §2.2).
The memo states 'The DA Territory is DE, MD, NJ and PA only (DA §1.12).'
The memorandum is addressed to the Partner. Each numbered issue sets out where it appears, why it matters, and a recommended fix.
Issues are labelled 'most significant first' with severity ratings. Section 1 flags immediate actions for the client and Quillon's counsel, with an order of approach.

The memo states that a notice sent now is late and not effective under §3.2, and that the DA does not renew automatically. The protective notice it suggests is framed as a request for relief, not a timely notice.
The memo states expressly that Velloran is not listed on Sched. 3.6 and is not covered by §6.4 or §7.1(d).
